transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. It’s so nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I’m not wasting your time, I know you must see people with much bigger problems. 

But I came in because... well, I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. It’s actually a little embarrassing to admit, if I'm being honest. My kitchen table is just covered with things right now—my husband’s appointment papers, flyers from church, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished to-do lists. I really do try to tackle it, but I just sit there looking at the piles, not knowing which thing I'm supposed to do first. And then, somehow, the whole day is just gone. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I’m explaining it okay.
Is this difficulty getting organized a change from how you used to be?

Oh, um... well, no, not really a change, I suppose. I mean, I don't want to sound like I've always been a mess, because I really have tried my best over the years! But... no, it's always been a bit of a struggle for me. 

Even when I was just a little girl, I remember my mother showing me my report cards. The teachers would always write such nice things first, you know, saying I was a bright girl... but then they would always add that I was careless. I was always forgetting my books or my homework. They had to constantly remind me to finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside for recess. I always felt so bad about it, because I really wanted to be a good student and please them. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
As an adult, have you often felt restless or like you have trouble sitting still?

Oh, restless? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I can sit and read my Bible or knit for quite a while, as long as I don't get distracted by something else I'm supposed to be doing. 

I'm definitely not one of those people who's always bouncing off the walls or talking a mile a minute. I know some folks can be a bit... much, but I always try to be polite and quiet, you know? I really don't think I have a problem with sitting still. I hope that's an okay answer... does that help at all?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Oh, depressed? Goodness, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I have so much to be thankful for, really. My husband is very good to me, and I have my church family... I try to count my blessings every day. 

I do get a little... well, maybe frustrated with myself sometimes, just because I can't seem to keep up with things the way I ought to. It makes me feel a bit silly, being my age and still struggling to just sort the mail. But I don't feel sad or hopeless or anything like that. I really try to keep a positive attitude! 

I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression. Is it normal to just be a little frustrated without being depressed?
Have you been having trouble with your memory?

Oh, my memory? Well... I don't think it's my memory, exactly. I mean, I know I just mentioned struggling to sort the mail and things like that, but I really don't want you to think my mind is going! I'm actually quite sharp, thank the Lord. 

I don't forget important things like my grandchildren's birthdays or recipes I've made for years. It's more just... well, little things slipping my mind if I'm trying to do too many things at once. Like, I might walk into the kitchen and forget what I went in there for, but I think everyone does that sometimes, don't they? 

I really don't think I have a bad memory, just a bit of a scattered brain sometimes. I hope that makes sense... I'm answering these questions alright, aren't I?
Do these difficulties with staying organized cause problems for you in more than one part of your life?

Oh, problems? Goodness, I wouldn't use the word *problems*, no. I mean, since I'm not working anymore, it's really just... well, just little things around the house. 

I always make sure my husband is taken care of, and I would never, ever let my little... organizational hiccups affect my volunteer work at the church or anything like that. I try very hard to keep things nice and proper for other people. It's really only my own personal things—like my sewing room or my own stacks of mail—that get a bit jumbled up. 

I really don't want you to think my whole life is in shambles! I manage quite well, all things considered. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?

Oh, worrying? No, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier, really. I mean, I care about things, of course—I want my family to be happy and healthy, and I want to do a good job with my church activities. But I don't sit around fretting all day, goodness no. 

I know some people get themselves into a real state over every little thing, but I just try to trust the Lord and take things one day at a time. I mean, I might get a little flustered if I misplace my glasses for the third time in a morning, but that's just a bit of annoyance, not real worry. 

I try to be a very peaceful person, mostly. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just don't want to give you the idea that I'm a nervous wreck or anything like that.
Before you retired, did being forgetful or disorganized ever cause trouble for you at work?

Oh, at work? Well... no, I wouldn't say it caused *trouble*. I was an administrative assistant for many years, and I always made sure my boss had what he needed. I mean, I was very dedicated. 

I suppose... well, sometimes I might have had to stay a little late to finish up some filing, or maybe I had to redo a letter if I missed a detail the first time around. But I always got it done! I never let anyone down. I just had to work a little harder sometimes to keep all the plates spinning, if that makes sense. 

I really prided myself on being a good employee. I hope that doesn't sound like I was incompetent? I always did my best, I promise.
Before age 12, did you often have trouble finishing schoolwork or keeping track of your things?

Oh, before I was twelve? Goodness, that's going back a ways! Well... I suppose I wouldn't say I had *trouble*, exactly. I was always a very happy little girl, and I loved school. 

I mean, if I'm being perfectly honest, I suppose my teachers did sometimes write on my report cards that I was... well, they said I was bright! They always said I was bright. But they might have also mentioned that I could be a little, oh, careless sometimes. Just little things, like maybe forgetting a book or a homework assignment here and there. 

And, well, sometimes they had to remind me to finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside for recess. But I was just so eager to play with the other children, you know? I didn't mean to be disobedient or anything like that. I was a good girl, really I was. I just got a little distracted by all the fun things happening around me. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student? I really did try my best to please my teachers.
Have these difficulties gotten noticeably worse in the past few years compared with how you used to be?

Well, I wouldn't say they've gotten *terribly* worse, but... well, yes, I suppose I have noticed a little bit of a change lately. Just in the last year or so. Maybe a year and three months? 

It's just that my husband has started needing a bit more help, you see. He has more doctor's appointments now, and I've been trying to keep track of his daily arrangements, and... well, it's just a lot of extra details to manage. I want to make sure he's well taken care of, of course! He's a wonderful man. But I suppose keeping all those new schedules straight on top of everything else has just been a little... tricky for me lately. 

I'm still managing, though! I just have to write a few more things down. I hope you don't think I'm complaining or failing him as a wife? I really do consider it a blessing to be able to care for him, it's just a bit more of an adjustment than I expected.
Because of these difficulties, do you need help managing the bills?

Oh, the bills? Well... I wouldn't say I *need* help, exactly. I've always been very responsible with our finances, you know? But... well, my daughter has been coming over a bit more often lately. She's such a sweet girl, so helpful. 

She's just been... oh, taking a little peek at the mail and the checkbook when she visits. Just double-checking things, she says. She started doing it with my husband's appointments, too. I think she just worries, you know how children are with their parents as we get a little older. She said she just wants to make sure I'm keeping everything straight, which I am! Mostly. I mean, I might have misplaced a statement once or twice, but nothing terrible. I hope that doesn't sound like I'm losing my touch? 

And, well, I did step down from leading the big spring gala at the senior center this year. I just told them I wanted to give someone else a turn! But... between you and me, it was just getting to be a bit too much to organize with everything else. I feel terrible about it, I really do. I hate to let people down. Do you think it's okay that I let my daughter help out a little bit? I don't want to be a burden to her.
Have you missed any bill payments recently?

Oh... oh dear. Well... I suppose I have to be completely honest with you, don't I? I... well, yes. I might have left a bill or two sitting under a stack of mail recently and... well, they were just a tiny bit late. I felt just awful about it! I usually pride myself on being so prompt. 

And, well, since we're talking about it... I suppose I've missed returning a few phone calls lately, too. And I've forgotten a couple of little errands I promised my daughter I’d run for her. She's so patient with me, but I just hate letting her down. Oh, and... well, more than once now, I’ve realized just a little too late that I never actually called to confirm one of my husband’s appointments. 

I really do try my absolute best, I promise you I do! It’s just... things seem to slip my mind a bit more than they used to. That’s normal when you have a lot on your plate, isn't it? I hope you don't think I'm becoming completely irresponsible...
Have you gotten lost while driving somewhere familiar?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I haven't gotten lost driving. I mean, I know my way around town like the back of my hand! I've lived here for... oh, just forever, it feels like. 

I suppose I might take a wrong turn every now and then, but who doesn't? Sometimes they close a road for construction, or... or I'm just enjoying the scenery and miss my turnoff. But I always figure it out right away! I just turn around at the next block. I certainly wouldn't say I get *lost*. 

I'm a very safe driver, I assure you. I always pay attention to the road. You believe me, don't you? I wouldn't want you to think I shouldn't be driving or anything like that. I'm perfectly capable of getting myself and my husband where we need to go!
Do you find yourself forgetting recent conversations?

Oh, no, thankfully not. I've always been a very good listener! If my daughter tells me about her day, or... or my husband and I are chatting, I remember what we talked about. 

I mean, I suppose if someone just mumbles something in passing I might not catch every single word, but I certainly don't forget actual conversations. My memory for that sort of thing is still quite sharp, I think. That's a good sign, isn't it? I always try so hard to give people my full attention when they speak to me. I'd just hate for anyone to think I didn't care about what they were saying!
Has your daughter told you that she thinks your memory or thinking has gotten worse?

Oh, goodness, no. My daughter hasn't said anything like that to me. She's... she's such a sweet girl, she wouldn't want to worry me. And really, I think she knows I'm just as sharp as ever! 

I mean, we all have our moments where we might forget a tiny detail here or there, don't we? Especially at my age. But she certainly hasn't sat me down and told me she's concerned about my thinking or my memory. We have lovely chats, and I always keep up just fine! 

You don't think she's said something to *you*, do you? I would just be so embarrassed if she felt she had to talk to someone else about me instead of coming to me directly. But no, I'm quite sure she thinks I'm doing just wonderfully.
Has your daughter told you that you seem more forgetful or more disorganized than you used to be?

Oh... well... I suppose... maybe she has mentioned something a bit like that. Not in a harsh way, of course! She's just trying to be helpful. But... well, she has started double-checking my bills and my calendar for my appointments. I think she just... she doesn't quite trust that I can keep everything straight on my own anymore. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly. I let her do it because I don't want to argue, and I suppose it's alright to accept a little help, isn't it? I just don't want to be a burden to her.

And, well, I did decide to step down from leading this big event we put on at the senior center. I actually had to give it up entirely. There were just... oh, so many little details, and I was having such a hard time keeping them all organized this year. But it's perfectly normal to want a little less responsibility at my age, don't you think? I just thought it would be best for everyone if I let someone else take the reins so I wouldn't mess it up.
Has a doctor told you that you have any brain or nerve problem, like a stroke, Parkinson’s disease, or a head injury?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I've been very blessed, really. My regular doctor has never mentioned anything about a stroke or... or Parkinson's, or anything to do with my nerves. 

I always make sure to go to all my annual checkups, you know, just to be on the safe side. I try very hard to be a good patient and take care of myself. That's the right thing to do, isn't it? I'd hate to let something like that slip by. But yes, thankfully, no head injuries or anything scary like that. I'm quite healthy in that department, which is such a relief!
Besides your daughter checking on things, have you had to stop handling the household finances on your own?

Well, no, not completely... I mean, I still try to keep an eye on things, of course. But... yes, as I mentioned, my daughter has taken to double-checking the bills. And my appointments, too. I think she just feels a little more comfortable if she looks them over, you know? It's not that I can't do it, I just... I suppose she doesn't entirely trust me to keep it all straight anymore without a little backup. Which is fine! It's so nice of her to help. 

And, like I said before, I did step away from leading that big event at the senior center. It just got to be a bit much, trying to juggle all those little details on my own. I didn't want to let anyone down, so I thought it was better to let someone else handle it. That was the responsible choice, wasn't it? I just think it's better to accept a little help when things get complicated, rather than make a mess of it all.
Are you still able to manage your medications on your own?

Oh, yes... yes, absolutely. I still do all of that myself. I have one of those... you know, those little plastic pill organizers with the days of the week on them? I'm very careful to sit down and fill it up every Sunday. 

I mean, occasionally I might have to stop and think for a second if I already took my morning pill, but... well, that happens to everyone from time to time, doesn't it? I'm really quite diligent about it, honestly. It's so important to follow the doctor's instructions, and I do try my very best to do exactly what I'm told. So, yes, I manage my medicines just fine on my own. That's a good thing, right?
Have you been having trouble learning new things?

Oh, learning new things? Um... no, I wouldn't say I have trouble, exactly. I mean, I don't really try to learn a lot of complicated new things these days, anyway. 

I suppose... well, if someone shows me how to use a new feature on my phone, it might take me a little longer to get the hang of it than it used to. But I always figure it out eventually! I just have to sit with it for a bit and really focus. That's perfectly normal for someone my age, isn't it? I don't think it's anything to worry about. I still love reading my books and keeping up with the news, so my mind is still working just fine in that regard. I'm doing okay, aren't I?
